transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, my head just doesn't stay on task anymore. It's like, I'll be doing inventory at work, or trying to study for this supervisor certification, and I just keep reading the same line over and over. Or I'll walk to the supply closet and completely forget what I went in there for. It's just getting really frustrating.
When did you first notice these concentration problems and memory lapses starting to happen?

It's been going on for about three years now. Yeah, right around three years. I think it really started when the contractor I work for changed our schedules. They switched us over to rotating evening and overnight shifts at some of the larger properties, and it's just been happening ever since then.
How is your sleep been since you started working those rotating evening and overnight shifts? Are you able to get enough sleep, and do you feel rested when you wake up?

My sleep has been pretty messed up for a long time now, honestly. Like, after an overnight shift, I'll get home and just lie there in bed. I'm tired, but I'm wired at the same time, so I can't just drift off. And... well, even when I do manage to sleep a decent number of hours, I wake up feeling like I barely rested at all.
Besides the trouble concentrating and sleeping, have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless over these past three years?

Yeah, I guess I have. Most days, I just feel... flat. It's like this heavy feeling that just kind of follows me around. I'll be pushing my cart down an empty hallway at work, or even just sitting at home with my family trying to act normal, and it's just there. It never really goes away.
On your days off when you're not working those rotating shifts, do you find that your sleep improves and you feel more rested, or does the sleep problem persist regardless of your schedule?

It doesn't really matter if I have the day off or not. The problem is still there. I mean, my body's just so out of whack from the schedule changes that even when I have a normal night to sleep, I still can't fall asleep easily. And I still wake up feeling exhausted. It's like my brain forgot how to actually rest.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your interest in things you normally enjoy doing, like hobbies or spending time with friends and family?

Not really, no. My appetite is pretty much the same as it's always been. I haven't noticed any changes there. 

And as for my family or things I like to do... I mean, I still want to spend time with them. I haven't lost interest in that stuff. It's just, like I said, I'm usually pretty exhausted when I'm around them because of the sleep stuff. But I still care about doing those things. I still want to be there.
Have you tried to get back to a regular sleep schedule, like going to bed and waking up at the same time every day, even on your days off? If so, what happened when you tried that?

I've tried, yeah. I mean, on my days off, I try to lay down at a normal time, like maybe 10 or 11 at night, to try and get back on a normal person's schedule. But... it just doesn't work. I just lay there staring at the ceiling. My body just won't shut down, no matter how hard I try to force a routine. So eventually I just give up and watch TV or something until I finally crash.
Looking back to when this all started three years ago, did the trouble sleeping come first, or did you notice the flat, heavy mood feeling starting around the same time as the sleep problems?

I think they kind of started around the same time. It's been going on for a while now, but yeah... most days I just feel like there's this heavy, flat feeling following me around. It doesn't really matter what I'm doing. Even when I'm just pushing my cart down an empty hallway at work, or sitting with my family trying to act normal, that heavy feeling is just... there. It's like a weight I can't shake off.

If you were able to somehow get your sleep completely back to normal—like if you could sleep deeply and wake up feeling truly rested every night—do you think that heavy, flat feeling you described would go away, or do you think it would still be there?

I don't really know for sure. I mean... I'd love to just get a good night's sleep, obviously. But... if I'm being honest, I think that heavy feeling would probably still be there. It just feels like it's a part of me now, you know? Like, the sleep stuff makes it harder to deal with, for sure, because I'm just so tired all the time. But even on the rare days where I do manage to get a few extra hours, that flat mood... it doesn't really lift. So, yeah, I think it would still be hanging around.

When you describe that heavy, flat feeling you have most days, does it include feelings of worthlessness or guilt about things in your life, or is it more just a lack of energy and motivation from being tired?

I think... yeah, there is definitely some of that worthlessness in there. It's not just being tired all the time. 

I mean, I look at where I'm at, and I keep telling myself that other guys would have adjusted by now, you know? They would have moved up or figured things out. But I'm still just... I'm just trying to make sure I don't miss small things at work. It just makes me feel like maybe I'm not cut out for anything more than this.

In these past three years, have there been any stretches of time—even just a few weeks or a month—where that heavy, flat feeling lifted and you felt more like your normal self, or has it been pretty consistently there the whole time?

No, not really. It's been pretty constant. Like I said, it's been going on for about three years now. It all started when the cleaning contractor switched us to rotating evening and overnight shifts at the larger buildings. Ever since then, it's just been this same heavy feeling, pretty much every day. I don't think I've had a break from it for more than maybe a day or two here and there, definitely not a few weeks.
